role.altitude: The programming director keeps planning and directing the on-air fundraising; writing pitch scripts and matching pledges to segments by hand shrink.
skills_to_grow: Reading pledge results per segment during a campaign
role.ambitious_version: A director who moves fundraising segments during the campaign to the slots that actually raise money.

tasks.short: Join the fundraising campaign planning, place on-air fundraising segments in the schedule, write pitch scripts, get them approved, direct the segments on air and review pledge results per segment.

steps.what: Programming director participates in planning the fundraising campaign with the fundraising team
Programming director places fundraising segments and breaks in the programme schedule
Programming director writes on-air pitch scripts and promos for the fundraising activities

loop.input: The campaign fact sheet (goal, what the money funds, thank-you gifts, how to give) and the segment length.
loop.output: Draft pitch scripts and promo texts per segment length.
loop.check: Every amount, gift, phone number and web address must match the fact sheet, or the line is marked; the director reads each script for what it promises and rewrites any line the fact sheet does not support.
loop.stop: One draft per segment type and fact sheet version; if rejected, the director writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template gives the call to action; each segment needs its own spoken story.

steps.what: Fundraising manager checks the final pitch scripts for the right offer and approves them
Programming director directs the fundraising segments on air with presenters
Programming director reviews pledges per segment to adjust the rest of the campaign schedule
Programming director moves the remaining fundraising segments in the scheduling system, keeping each approved script unchanged

approvals.approved_version: pitch scripts as approved by the fundraising manager in s4; a change to amounts, gifts or how to give needs a new approval

tasks.design: Fundraising segments are placed in the station's scheduling system ({OTHER}) instead of a separate spreadsheet. A bounded step drafts pitch scripts from the campaign fact sheet, with every amount, gift and number checked against it, and the fundraising manager approves the final scripts. During the campaign a dashboard joins pledge times from the {CRM} with the actual broadcast times in the as-run log, so the director sees which segments raised money and moves the remaining segments in the scheduling system. A moved segment keeps its approved script; any change of wording goes back through drafting and the manager's approval before air. Directing on air stays with the director.
tasks.previous_blocker: Pledges were matched to segments by hand after the campaign, too late to change anything.
tasks.enabler_now: Pledge records carry timestamps and as-run logs record actual broadcast times.
tasks.still_hard: Making an on-air appeal that moves people.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which story makes listeners pick up the phone.

ambition.what: Move fundraising segments during the campaign based on pledges per segment.

tasks.altitude: The director gets results during the campaign instead of after; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Which programmes and times bring pledges.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft spoken scripts whose amounts and numbers can be checked against a fact sheet.
AI-made text published to inform the public needs disclosure unless a person reviews it under editorial responsibility.
Fundraising appeals on air follow national broadcasting rules on appeals and sponsorship.

assumptions: Boundary: from campaign planning to schedule adjustments; taking pledges and processing gifts belong to the fundraising team and are outside.
Input contract for s6: pledge records with time and channel from the fundraising team's {CRM}; actual broadcast times from the playout as-run log; results use actual air times, not planned slots.
Input contract for s3: a campaign fact sheet kept by the fundraising manager.

Planning meetings, directing on air and moving segments keep their full time. s2 is sized at 8 because a campaign places a handful of segments; s2 keeps 80 because placing them in the scheduling system replaces a separate spreadsheet. s3 keeps 70 because the director rewrites what the fact sheet does not support. s6 keeps 40 for reading results and deciding moves; the join of pledge times to as-run times is integration code.
unknowns: How many fundraising campaigns per year.
Whether pledge records carry a usable timestamp.
research_questions: Do segments moved during the campaign raise more?

already_counted.description: Programming director edits drafted pitch scripts.
Programming director reads the pledge dashboard during the campaign.

incremental.description: Programming director checks the fact sheet link to scripts at each campaign.
Station IT keeps the join of pledge times to the as-run log working between campaigns.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the {CRM} gives only daily pledge totals, so the join cannot match segments and s6 stays as today (10.0); high: pledge times join the as-run log as designed (14.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
